COMMENT:  
Sections reveal a moderately cellular glial neoplasm with a fibrillary
matrix. Tumor cells exhibit round to oval nuclei with finely dispersed
chromatin and elongated cytoplasmic extensions. Numerous perivascular
pseudorosettes are evident. There is no necrosis, and mitotic figures
are rare.  
The following immunohistochemical stains were performed at USC and
evaluated on block B1:
- GFAP:          Positive staining in tumor cells, highlighting
perivascular pseudorosettes.
- EMA:               Dot-like positivity in tumor cells.
- H3K27me3:          Retained expression in tumor cells.
- Ki-67:                Labeling index estimated at less than 2%.
Overall, the features are consistent with a posterior fossa ependymoma,
favor RELA fusion-positive, CNS WHO grade 2. Further genetic
characterization will be conducted using the USC NGS panel, with a
separate report from the USC Clinical Cancer Genomics Laboratory to
follow, and an addendum will be issued if clinically warranted.

Clinical History
The patient is a 59-year-old woman presenting with headaches and balance
disturbances, found to have a 3.2 cm enhancing mass in the posterior
fossa on MRI with increased T2/FLAIR signal and reduced T1 signal.
Radiographically, the differential diagnosis included ependymoma,
medulloblastoma, and metastasis. Additionally, subtle enhancement in the
left cerebellar hemisphere was noted. She now undergoes resection of the
mass.
